items.summary: Carolyn Marvin, a semi-retired University of Pennsylvania communications professor and former author of When Old Technologies Were New, blocks UberEats food delivery robots on busy sidewalks as protest against their presence in public space. After being handcuffed for blocking a robot she was holding out food to, Marvin intends to contest her disorderly conduct ticket. She argues the robots threaten jobs and pose hazards to people with mobility issues, while others worry about denying paid orders. Onlookers react mixed—some cheer her as 'the queen,' citing distrust of AI; passing children are drawn by the robots' humanizing Halloween graphics added by Avride, which operates nearly 1,000 machines across campuses and cities like Jersey City and Austin. Marvin says she wants people to know they have a say in whether private robots belong on public streets.
items.title: Professor Blocks Food Delivery Robots in Philadelphia Protest

items.summary: Thailand paused construction on 49 datacentre projects and approval decisions on 117 more in September 2026, amid concerns about insufficient regulatory detail. The shift follows a broader regional reassessment: Indonesia halted one project over missing permits, while Singapore had earlier imposed a moratorium from 2019 to 2022 for water and electricity use. Wood Mackenzie estimates Johor’s datacentres already consume 24% of the state’s power, potentially rising to 40% by 2035, and that operational sites need about 675m cubic meters of water per day. Analysts warn of grid bottlenecks and uneven benefit-sharing as investment accelerates amid AI-driven demand.
items.title: Southeast Asia Pauses Datacentre Expansion Over Resource Strain

items.summary: Cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was targeted in a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million. The attacker used the bank's own account rather than customers' accounts and converted funds into USDC and USDT stablecoins, leaving customer assets unaffected. Arkéa suspended certain systems and reassured clients there is no impact on their assets while operations return to normal.
items.title: Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider

items.summary: CTM360 reports that fraudulent reward portals and fake gift card giveaways are surging globally, luring users with celebrity endorsements and a deceptive human verification step. Analysts identified more than 1,000 incidents impersonating brands such as PlayStation, Sephora, SHEIN, Walmart, and Amazon. In every flow tested by CTM360, no reward was ever delivered; instead the campaigns collect personal information, generate app installs, and enroll users in recurring mobile subscriptions for affiliate commissions.
items.title: CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands

items.summary: A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a lawsuit brought by homeowner Ambrose Conroy over an unfinished and unpermitted Solar Roof installation. Tesla had already conceded breach of contract, warranty violation and negligence; the court added liability on its discovery failures, ordering two monetary sanctions before ruling that it acted willfully by withholding internal records such as Microsoft Teams messages and quality reports. The roof was never inspected or powered, and a settlement offer of $5,000 drew sharp criticism. Tesla is now petitioning the California Court of Appeal to freeze the case, arguing the sanction violates due process; a trial readiness conference is set for December 4.
items.title: California Judge Holds Tesla Liable for Solar Roof Fraud

items.summary: Researchers at Middle Technical University in Baghdad report a solar-panel cooling system that could raise efficiency in hot climates, according to Results in Engineering. The design pairs an evaporative cellulose pad behind the panel with intermittent water spraying on its front surface when it reaches 42–45 °C. Mahmood says dry air “provides the ideal thermodynamic environment for highly efficient latent evaporative cooling.” In testing during Baghdad’s hottest hours, the best configuration dropped panel temperature by 29.7 °C and improved electrical efficiency about 20 percent. KAUST researchers note net energy benefits, water use, and costs should be weighed beyond temperature alone; Mahmood admits fan and pump power may offset gains in small prototypes but could scale commercially.
items.title: Iraqi Researchers Cool Solar Panels With Water Spray

items.summary: Two Massachusetts cranberry bogs in Kingston and Plymouth are the country's — perhaps world's — first to grow berries beneath operating solar panels, marking the region's second season of harvest under them. Growers navigate equipment around metal poles shaded by photovoltaic arrays mounted 10 feet off the ground. The projects were built by Greenbacker Renewables with Distributed Energy Infrastructure and managed by consultant Iain Ward. Massachusetts has promoted agrivoltaics to reach net-zero emissions by 2050, offering incentives for dual-use solar on farmland that cannot be developed because cranberry bogs are protected wetlands.
items.title: Massachusetts bogs become nation's first cranberry solar farms

items.summary: The article reports that several U.S. hydrogen development projects have stalled amid funding uncertainty under the Trump administration and weak demand. In November 2024, the Biden administration had announced up to $2.2 billion in award commitments for two Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs out of a total of $7 billion across seven hubs. The MACH2 hub received a $750 million Department of Energy award, while ARCH2 was expected to receive $925 million. Air Products cancelled its $4.5 billion Louisiana project after reporting approximately $2.9 billion in pretax charges, and Exxon Mobil paused a Baytown facility that could produce up to 1 billion cubic feet of blue hydrogen per day; the firm said it had invested around $500 million and cited weak customer demand. Tom Torres stated he does not think the hubs are happening until evidence suggests otherwise.
items.title: US Hydrogen Hubs Stall on Funding Cuts and Weak Demand

items.summary: As climate negotiators gather for the annual United Nations summit, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change faces gridlock and funding shortfalls. The panel suspended its mid-October meeting without approving next year's budget or a report timetable. More than 100 scientists signed an Oct. 19 open letter urging adequate resources. Bob Kopp of Rutgers University said U.S. funding cuts likely stalled the process, though the country still contributes about 7.5 percent and one-third historically. Davide Faranda warned climate information could be weaponized if collaboration breaks down. The IPCC will resume online in December after COP31 begins next week in Antalya, Turkey.
items.title: IPCC Gridlock and Funding Shortfalls Loom Before COP31

items.summary: Electric truck maker Workhorse is introducing its W56 Class 5 and 6 electric trucks to Canada through a new agreement with Tristan Fleet Management, marking the company's first-ever Canadian dealer partnership. The deal adds sales, parts, repair, and round-the-clock roadside support nationwide. Workhorse highlights years of Canadian deployments since 2021 and cites high fuel costs as boosting demand for electrification.
items.title: Workhorse W56 Electric Trucks Enter Canada via New Dealer Deal

items.summary: Lighthouse, a subsidiary of Difare Group, inaugurated the 82 MW Faro de San Marcos solar plant on Nov. 5 in Ecuador’s Santa Elena province. The developer says it is the country’s largest operational and privately owned solar facility, with more than 105,000 bifacial modules across 49.3 hectares. It began commercial operation ahead of a first-quarter-2027 schedule; company estimates put annual output at about 106 GWh.
items.title: Ecuador’s Largest Private Solar Plant Begins Commercial Operation

items.summary: At this year’s IEC general meeting, officials discussed how rapid technological change is challenging traditional conformity assessment for standards-based products. Wolfram Zeitz of the IECEE and IECRE systems noted that development speed has accelerated sharply, creating uncertainty among consumers about rushed or unverified certification. Henrike Gördes of DKE added that software updates can alter product behavior after testing, so assessment must follow a product throughout its lifecycle rather than only at launch. Progress is underway: CASCO collaborates on ISO/IEC 42007 for AI conformity schemes, and new pilot programs with IEC TC 62 explore medical device evaluation. DKE advocates shifting toward continuous, cyclical approaches to better reflect evolving digital products while preserving international consensus as a foundation of trust.
items.title: IEC Officials Address Trust Challenges in AI and New Technology Standards

items.summary: At its annual general meeting on Saturday, National Trust members voted overwhelmingly—53,256 for and 4,094 against—to seek a new bank that prioritises biodiversity protection and climate action. The resolution instructs the charity to launch a competitive tendering process, though insiders suggest it may take at least a year. Sandy Nairne warned the result is not binding on trustees. Proposer Drew James argued Barclays undermines conservation by financing fossil fuels, while Restore Trust’s Cornelia van der Poll called the vote a distraction from maintaining historic buildings and countryside.
items.title: National Trust votes for ethical banking partner

items.summary: A Great Lakes-based non-profit is preparing as reports suggest the Trump administration may plan four sealed-pod underwater datacenters off Maine and Alaska, though no projects are currently proposed in the region. Activists warn of heat-driven algal blooms and thermal shock from even a 2-5F rise, while Microsoft says it has no plans to deploy an underwater unit at this time. New York’s moratorium ends mid-2027; Ohio recently denied wastewater discharge after public outcry.
items.title: Great Lakes non-profit prepares for underwater datacenters

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin expanded temporary administration over three additional JTI businesses on Saturday, following a Thursday decree placing the Russian assets of Japan Tobacco International under Industrial Assets. The tobacco group is among foreign firms losing control as Moscow tightens grip on overseas-owned assets. JTI said it was assessing options and prioritising employees; Anton Pivovarov of Industrial Assets said production would continue without disruption.
items.title: Putin Expands Temporary Administration of Japan Tobacco Assets in Russia

items.summary: Jefferies' Christopher Wood warns that a slowdown in US artificial intelligence spending could weaken economic growth and shift expectations toward Federal Reserve rate cuts, potentially supporting gold. With prices consolidating around $3,800–4,000 per ounce, he cautions investors to avoid treating the range as an assured buying opportunity.
items.title: Jefferies Sees AI Spending Slowdown Could Fuel Gold Rally

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party will hold a special hawan and puja at its national headquarters in New Delhi on Sunday, November 8, to mark the 99th birthday of veteran leader Lal Krishna Advani. The ceremony includes prayers for his health followed by a presentation about his political journey. BJP president Nitin Nabin and Union Minister Piyush Goyal are expected to speak, according to party sources.
items.title: BJP Holds Special Hawan for Advani's 99th Birthday

items.summary: A CGTN opinion piece argues that Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has failed to correct a year-old remark linking a possible 'Taiwan contingency' to Japan's collective self-defense. Cao Cong, the article's author, states Tokyo neither withdrew nor corrected the remarks and describes them as an error connecting China's internal affairs to military action. The piece frames this alongside what it calls accelerating remilitarization: a fiscal 2026 defense budget exceeding 9 trillion yen (about $56.79 billion), deployments of Type-25 missiles, revised arms-export rules and the creation of a National Intelligence Bureau on July 31. It cites former officials Yukio Hatoyama and Takeshi Iwaya as calling for correction and urges Japan to withdraw its remarks and curb military expansion. The views are attributed to Cao Cong and not presented as CGTN's own, with an editor's note stating the article reflects his opinions only.
items.title: Japan's Taiwan remarks and military buildup strain regional peace, CGTN commentator says

items.summary: Chinese white dolphins, called the "giant pandas of the sea," are among the rarest marine animals in China. In Xiamen, Fujian Province, rescue teams work to protect injured and stranded dolphins while ecological restoration improves their natural habitat.
items.title: Xiamen Rescue Teams Protect China's Rarest Marine Mammals

items.summary: A CERES-2 Y3 carrier rocket launched at 7:37 am Beijing time on November 7, 2026, from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. It delivered four satellites into a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit. Developed by Galactic Energy, the medium-lift vehicle uses three solid stages plus a liquid upper stage, with an approximate liftoff mass of 100 tonnes and a payload capacity of 1.3 tonnes to a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit.
items.title: Galactic Energy's CERES-2 Y3 Rocket Launches Four Satellites from Jiuquan

items.summary: The ninth China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on November 5, 2026 and runs through November 10. A CGTN commentator argues the event's value lies beyond high-profile innovations such as laparoscopic surgical robots and prototype 6G terminals; instead it showcases upstream industrial chains linking suppliers to end-product developers under one roof. The article presents this 'point-to-sector-to-chain' layout, seen in a semiconductor exhibition area gathering material suppliers, equipment makers, chip designers and downstream firms, as evidence of the expo's evolution from product display toward full-chain collaboration.
items.title: CIIE 2026 reframes expo around full industrial chains, not single exhibits

items.summary: Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire from a car in Kraków’s Main Market Square, police said. The perpetrator was shot by officers during the confrontation and is being transported to hospital; no motive has been announced as investigations continue.
items.title: Kraków Square Shooting Leaves Five Dead

items.summary: No clear winner emerged from New Zealand's Saturday election, with preliminary results showing National on 42 seats and Labour on 36. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon conceded a hard-fought race while opposition leader Chris Hipkins refused to concede, calling the next government's shape uncertain for a while. With over 99% of votes counted, coalition negotiations are expected later in the month.
items.title: New Zealand Election Yields No Clear Winner as Coalition Talks Loom

items.summary: Stephen Miller, Donald Trump’s incoming White House chief of staff, pledged “total devotion” and absolute loyalty to the president after his appointment. The move follows midterm losses for Republicans in the Senate and 42 seats in the House, amid concern over a hardline immigration agenda that has drawn dismay from Democrats and some Republicans.
items.title: Stephen Miller Pledges Devotion as Trump Names Him Chief of Staff

items.summary: Ben Shelton beat hometown favourite Luca Van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 to reach the Paris Masters final, his third ATP 1000 final. The American recovered from a first-set stumble and unforced errors, winning long rallies before breaking for the set lead. He becomes the first American finalist since Jack Sock in 2017, aiming for his third ATP 1000 title on Sunday.
items.title: Shelton Defeats Van Assche in Paris Masters Semifinal

items.summary: New Zealand won 43-21 against Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday, extending their unbeaten record in the Southern Hemisphere. Ten tries were scored across both sides amid errors and yellow cards. Beauden Barrett reached a test tally of 50 with two tries, while Damian McKenzie kicked four conversions. The result kept New Zealand level with South Africa on 20 points at the top of the standings, as Scotland suffered another defeat in their long winless run against them.
items.title: New Zealand beat Scotland 43-21 in Nations Championship

items.summary: A shooting near the main market square of Krakow, southern Poland, killed at least five people on Saturday, local police said. A car from which shots were fired entered the square around 3 pm (1400 GMT), according to a Reuters spokesperson who relayed reports received by police. The perpetrator was shot and is being taken to a hospital. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed he was informed by the interior ministry as the story continued.
items.title: Shooting in Krakow Kills at Least Five

items.summary: Millions now use AI chatbots as a news source, with a 2026 Reuters Institute survey of more than 90,000 people worldwide finding that 10% turn to them weekly. Media leaders argue this undermines journalism: DW's Barbara Massing said quality reporting has become 'largely invisible,' and Julia Becker called the old traffic exchange broken. German broadcasters ARD and RTL joined publishers in October calling for stronger copyright protections; The New York Times sued Brave Software, while a February coalition urged rules giving publishers control over AI copying. Experts like Martin Senftleben suggest existing EU law may allow collective payment without new legislation.
items.title: Media Groups Push AI Companies for Payment and Copyright Control

items.summary: Far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon is set to present his party France Unbowed's new manifesto, L'Avenir en commun (The Future in Common), at a rally in Le Bourget on Saturday. The document places ecological transformation among its main priorities and proposes replacing administrative regions with eco-regions focused on water management, alongside strengthening environmental protections in the constitution. Mélenchon currently polls around 18%, trailing Marine Le Pen between 35% and 37%. His manifesto has drawn criticism from opponents, including National Rally's Le Pen, who called it a plan to dismantle France. The presentation comes as protests continue across the country over wages and public services. Organisers estimated turnout at about 1.6 million people, though the interior ministry put the figure at 575,000 demonstrators. The manifesto has been published without a detailed financial breakdown but will be supplemented by around 50 documents detailing its measures.
items.title: Mélenchon Unveils New Party Manifesto Amid French Protests

items.summary: Reza Pahlavi, son of Iran's last shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi, received a 'Freedom Prize' from the Friedrich Naumann Foundation at St Paul's Church in Frankfurt on Saturday. Around 18,000 people rallied to support him, according to police. Rights groups say thousands were killed in January protests. Critics accuse him of supporting Israel and not distancing himself from his father's rule; some parties boycotted the event.
items.title: Iranian Opposition Leader Receives Freedom Prize in Frankfurt

items.summary: A gunman opened fire in the Main Square of Kraków, killing at least five people and injuring more than a dozen. The municipal government said the shooting occurred there; a firefighter spokesperson told Polsat News that the perpetrator fired from a passing car before being shot by police officers who are now transporting him to hospital. Emergency services remain on scene across several locations as authorities investigate.
items.title: Shooting on Kraków's Main Square Kills at Least Five

items.summary: Who Gives A Crap confirmed that an unauthorised party accessed customer data held by a US-based marketing software provider, the company said in a statement. The breach exposed names, contact details and total spend, but not payment details or passwords. Affected customers were located in Australia, the UK and the US; Canadian customers' data was not accessed.
items.title: Who Gives A Crap Confirms Customer Data Breach

items.summary: Burhanettin Duran, Turkey's communications director, warned at the TRT World Forum that technology companies are increasingly controlling global information flows through algorithms. He argued these systems replace editorial judgment and threaten media independence, national sovereignty and cultural identity. Duran stressed journalism cannot survive on visibility alone, calling for financial support and ethical principles to guide digital platforms.
items.title: Turkish Communications Director Warns Tech Giants Threaten Media Independence

items.summary: New Zealand's general election produced a razor-thin result with no clear path to government for weeks. On the count of ordinary ballots, National edged Labour 29.37% to 29.22%, giving an opposition bloc just one seat over the 66 needed for a majority. About 700,000 special votes remain to be processed and could change the balance of power. Leaders said results would take time; Chris Hipkins told supporters it would take
items.title: New Zealand election outcome hangs on special votes

items.summary: Pedro Sanchez said Saturday that the Nov. 29 general elections would prove Spain is ruled domestically, not by Washington, Tel Aviv, Buenos Aires or Moscow. Speaking in Tarragona, he vowed to resist far-right influence and defended rejecting Trump's demand for defense spending equal to 5% of GDP, prioritizing education, health care, social care and pensions instead.
items.title: Spanish premier vows Spain is governed from within

items.summary: Heavy rain on Saturday flooded tens of thousands of displaced people's tents across war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving them without shelter. The Hamas-run government media office reported that about 70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day, and noted the collapse of dozens of cracked walls and roofs, which caused injuries. Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP his teams received more than 1,500 calls during the night for urgent assistance after their tents flooded, explaining that the agency is operating without any equipment or capabilities.
items.title: Heavy Rains Flood Tents, Displace Thousands in Gaza

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a 12-day tour of South America, arriving in Uruguay three weeks after lung tumor surgery and describing himself as being "in fairly good shape." The 71-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. In Montevideo he greeted sparse crowds before lamenting the country's high suicide rates and calling for accessible healthcare. His tour is seen as a homecoming to his Peruvian roots.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Opens South American Tour Amid Cancer Recovery

items.summary: Houston Mayor John Whitmire directed city police to limit cooperation with federal immigration officials, citing a need to reduce community fear and anxiety after months of public outcry following an ICE officer's fatal shooting. The policy change follows Democratic midterm victories in Texas and breaks from the approach of Republican Governor Greg Abbott, who lost re-election.
items.title: Houston Mayor Orders Police to Limit ICE Cooperation

items.summary: After losing his reelection first round, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva took his first selfie on October 7, three days after being defeated by Flávio Bolsonaro. The move launched a social media campaign that grew a WhatsApp channel from 53,000 to 10.5 million followers and helped Lula win the election with 51.7% versus Bolsonaro’s 48.2%. Campaign figures noted each of Bolsonaro’s posts averaged 448,000 interactions while Lula’s averaged just 102,000. The article frames the selfie as a symbolic turning point in an otherwise poorly organized campaign that had lost on social media.
items.title: Lula’s Selfie Sparked a Digital Comeback After Losing Brazil’s First Round

items.summary: Ten months after María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela, observers increasingly see a political transition underway. Historian Margarita López Maya now believes the opposition leadership needed to drive democratization has arrived. Analysts agree her arrival signals an early presidential campaign and marks the start of transition. Opinion polls show 60% support for alternation, though no election date is set; Machado favors July 2027 while U.S. officials point further out. Constitutional uncertainty remains as ruling figures avoid declaring Maduro's absence from office. Experts like Carlos Valero warn that wanting change does not guarantee achieving it.
items.title: Venezuela's transition gains momentum after Machado's return

items.summary: Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi announced Friday that Japan will strengthen educational programs for U.S. troops in Okinawa following a robbery and murder allegedly committed by a Marine last month. The government, with the United States, agreed to incorporate prefectural input into briefing materials before deployment.
items.title: Japan Expands Education Programs for U.S. Troops in Okinawa After Robbery-Murder

items.summary: The article is a festive guide for Diwali 2026, which falls on Sunday, November 8. It opens with reflections on the festival’s themes of light overcoming darkness, family reunion, hope and new beginnings, then offers practical information: Lakshmi Puja timings in Mumbai (6:27 pm to 8:27 pm) and Delhi (5:54 pm to 7:50 pm), plus regional origins tied to Rama, Krishna, Mahavira and Guru Hargobind Sahib. The bulk of the piece is a large collection of greetings for family, friends, colleagues and social media, followed by inspirational quotes and Instagram captions. It closes with advice on celebrating more thoughtfully — using clay diyas instead of plastic lights, natural rangoli colors and reusable decorations to reduce smoke and protect air quality.
items.title: Diwali 2026 Greetings, Dates and Eco-Friendly Celebrations Guide

items.summary: After Democrats secured majorities in both chambers of Congress, party leaders are preparing a fast legislative agenda targeting President Donald Trump's policies. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the party would 'get out of the gate fast,' prioritizing reversal of Medicaid cuts, restoration of Affordable Care Act tax credits and ending what he called the 'reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.' Chuck Schumer added Democrats could continue pushing even if vetoed, with early bipartisan signs on ACA subsidies. Trump retains his veto power, and most legislation still faces a 60-vote Senate threshold that complicates passage.
items.title: Democrats Prepare Legislative Push Against Trump on Healthcare, Iran and Tariffs

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi sidestepped questions about the Gandhi family's control of her party and nepotism allegations during a Guardian interview, saying leadership should be decided by the party itself. The newspaper described her response as skirting over the issue while noting many remained unconvinced after repeated electoral defeats under Rahul Gandhi. She maintained Congress could still challenge the BJP but declined to address its decline directly. The conversation also touched on Indira Gandhi's 1975 Emergency, which Sonia called a mistake, and recalled Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991 as personal trauma.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Deflects Nepotism Charges Amid Congress Struggles

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath said on Saturday that those who ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to a lathicharge should apologise before visiting the Ram Mandir. He directed an apparent swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, scheduled to visit the temple on December 12. The report is by Aastha Jha of The Times of India.
items.title: UP CM Yogi Demands Apology Before Akhilesh's Ram Temple Visit

items.summary: Samir Arora's Helios Mid Cap Fund added shares of Aurobindo Pharma worth Rs 42.74 crore to its portfolio in October, along with Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses and PVR Inox. It increased its holding in One97 Communication (Paytm) to 5.10 lakh shares from 4.83 lakh, raised Multi Commodity Exchange of India by 51,430 shares, and added Ace Vector as the largest addition among 16 other stocks. The fund's assets under management stood at Rs 2,421 crore as of October 31, 2026, with a CAGR of 20.51% since its March 13, 2025 launch.
items.title: Helios Mid Cap Fund Adds Aurobindo Pharma, Paytm and Others

items.summary: The 19th annual CNO Financial Indianapolis Monumental Marathon, held in 2026, offers live tracking through the official app and online leaderboards. Runners from all 50 US states and more than 35 countries are expected to compete across a full marathon, half marathon and 5K on November 7. The event features an opening ceremony at 7:30 am, with races starting at 8 am or later along a flat downtown course.
items.title: Indianapolis Marathon Announces Race Schedule and Live Tracking Options

items.summary: Kerala-born Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, becoming the first Indian-American and first South Asian elected to lead the city. Incumbent Karen Bass conceded, pledging a smooth transition; she becomes the first LA mayor in two decades to lose re-election, after her term was marked by the Palisades Fire. Raman, an urban planner who returned from India in 2010 and served on the City Council since 2020, campaigned on housing accessibility, homelessness management and municipal services. She entered the race at the last minute, angering parts of the Democratic establishment. Her victory is framed amid wider Indian-American electoral gains, with a 5.5 million-strong community seeing several elected officials nationwide.
items.title: Nithya Raman Wins Los Angeles Mayoral Race as First Indian-American Mayor

items.summary: A confrontation erupted outside Abhishek Banerjee's residence in Kolkata after Trinamool Congress workers put up birthday hoardings, pitting TMC and BJP supporters against each other. The clash involved torn posters and destroyed placards, with escalating tensions despite Banerjee attempting to mediate. Kolkata Police intervened for nearly two hours while Banerjee had an altercation with officers.
items.title: Birthday Hoardings Spark Clash Outside Banerjee's Kolkata Home

items.summary: Malini Awasthi, a folk singer, took part in a session at the Panchayat Ayodhya conclave organised by the India Today Group. During the event, an AI-based animated Ramayan film produced by Aaj Tak was showcased and released. Awasthi appreciated its devotional music, lyrical composition, and visuals, highlighting how technology brings creative ideas to life through scenes like the return of Lord Ram and the Bharat Milap. The conclave also featured Yogi Adityanath addressing Deepotsav in Ayodhya about security, infrastructure, tourism progress, and calling for apologies from those who disrespected the city.
items.title: Folk singer Malini Awasthi praises AI animated Ramayan film at Ayodhya conclave

items.summary: The Conversation has published an article listing the five novels on the Booker Prize 2026 shortlist, describing each as written by its contributor. Luke Kennard's Black Bag is called a campus comedy inspired by a 1967 Oregon State University experiment; M John Harrison's The End of Everything imagines alien-induced collapse on the Kent coast and quotes his own writing about piling up real facts to reveal something unreal; Elizabeth Strout's The Things We Never Say follows Artie Dam, a Massachusetts Bay high school teacher nominated for the prize three times before; Marlon James's The Disappearers is set in Jamaica from 1988 to 2005 and concerns gay men who vanish without notice; and Rebecca Perry's debut May We Feed The King tells of a person obsessed with a medieval king remembered only for his faults. All five entries are presented as selections meant to inspire readers across different tastes.
items.title: The Conversation names a diverse Booker Prize 2026 shortlist

items.summary: PVR INOX Ltd issued a clarification after Karnataka's food safety authorities ordered the closure of a juice counter at its Forum Mall multiplex in Bengaluru. A viral video alleged staff reused disposable cups, prompting widespread criticism. PVR denied reusing them, saying the damaged, leaking glasses were set aside and an internal investigation found no process deviation. The health department cited multiple violations and issued a notice.
items.title: PVR INOX Clarifies Cup Reuse Allegations After Karnataka Closure

items.summary: On Saturday, Ayodhya celebrated the 10th edition of Deepotsav with more than 30 lakh diyas set to illuminate 56 ghats along the banks of the Saryu River. Thousands gathered at the illuminated ghats amid cultural performances and a light-and-sound show depicting Ramayana episodes. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attended; CM Adityanath addressed the crowd after worshipping Lord Ram and Goddess Janaki, recalling decades of struggle in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.
items.title: Ayodhya Deepotsav Marks 10th Edition With Over 30 Lakh Diyas

items.summary: Police recovered decomposed bodies of the accused cab driver Indusekar alias Sekar’s wife and mother-in-law from Yercaud forest area in Tamil Nadu’s Salem district, marking three recoveries so far in the alleged seven-member killings. Police suspect the murders occurred over 15 to 20 days amid domestic disputes, with possible use of sedatives still under investigation. Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge said police were questioning the accused’s minor daughter and expected more information within two to three days.
items.title: Karnataka Police Recover Third and Fourth Bodies in Bengaluru Cab Driver Murders

items.summary: In an edited extract from her memoir published by The Guardian, Sonia Gandhi recounts urging husband Rajiv Gandhi to refuse the prime ministership after Indira Gandhi was assassinated on October 31, 1984. Describing herself as overwhelmed by anger and anguish at his hospital meeting, she reportedly told him “They will kill you,” while he replied: “They will kill me anyway.”
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls pleading with Rajiv not to become PM

items.summary: Election authorities report that Hyderabad district generated and distributed about 12.54 lakh notices during SIR 2026, with the final electoral rolls scheduled for release on November 11 after hearings concluded on November 5.
items.title: Hyderabad Finalises Electoral Rolls for November 11

items.summary: The Bombay High Court quashed Maharashtra government notifications and show-cause notices seeking to acquire 84 hectares of Tata Power Company Limited land in Pune for a private Ayurvedic wellness project, reported Bar and Bench. The court set aside the March 2025 notification designating the area an industrial zone near Thokarwadi Dam, citing that it serves as the catchment area for TPCL’s hydroelectric operations. A bench of Justices Manish Pitale and Shreeram V Shirsat noted the land supports a 75-megawatt Bhivpuri Hydro Station and proposed 1,000-megawatt pumped storage project.
items.title: Bombay High Court Quashes Maharashtra Land Acquisition for Ayurvedic Project

items.summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee challenged the BJP on Saturday after Abhishek Banerjee, her Diamond Harbour constituency colleague and three-time MP, alleged that BJP-backed miscreants accompanied by police personnel attacked his residence in Kalighat around 2 am or 3 am. Condemning what she called atrocities and intimidation amid restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Mamata 'dared' the BJP to use its bulldozers against her, telling police: 'If you have the courage, come and run your bulldozers over my body.' She said the incident reflected lawlessness in the state, accused the party of hypocrisy for holding Save Democracy rallies while blocking pujas at her Patuapara home, warned officers to stay neutral or she would fight them, threatened to approach the Supreme Court, and called a minute's silence. PTI reported the statements.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee Defies BJP With Bulldozer Threat After MP's Home Attack

items.summary: In Mumbai, a 26-year-old physiotherapist from Mulund was allegedly kidnapped, assaulted and robbed inside an under-construction building in Vikhroli. On November 4 around 3:30 PM he took a Rapido ride to meet a female friend before being ambushed near Raj Plaza. The gang stripped him of his gold chain, earrings and silver bracelet, filmed the act on a mobile phone, seized his wallet with debit and credit cards, forced PIN disclosure and coerced online transfers from relatives' accounts. After withdrawing Rs45,000 at an ATM they returned his cards but threatened fatal consequences if he reported them.
items.title: Physiotherapist Abducted and Robbed in Vikhroli; Two Arrested, Four Hunted

items.summary: A video of an elderly woman watching Nitesh Tiwari's film 'Ramayana' in a South-dubbed version with 3D glasses has gone viral for her smiling reaction. The article notes the film received positive reviews and collected Rs. 64.85 crore on day one, rising to Rs. 112.90 crore over two days per Sacnilk.
items.title: Elderly Woman's Adorable Reaction to Ramayana Goes Viral

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government announced a hike in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state employees, aided educational institutions and urban local bodies, raising the rate to 63 percent. The revised DA takes effect from July 1, 2026, paid with November salaries. Arrears for July to October 2026 will be credited to General Provident Fund accounts after tax deductions; NPS employees receive 10 percent in Tier-I pension accounts and the remaining 90 percent via Public Provident Fund or National Savings Certificates. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also handed appointment letters to over 4,500 newly selected sub-inspectors and Platoon Commanders under Mission Rozgar on November 6.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh raises Dearness Allowance to 63 percent ahead of Diwali

items.summary: Foreign institutional investors bought more than the Rs 45,162 crore withdrawn by overseas investors in October, reversing recent outflows. FIIs were net buyers across all five trading sessions, extending their buying streak to a second consecutive week after a 10-week selling spell. Domestic institutions turned net sellers for the first time in 12 weeks, offloading Rs 24,197 crore as they booked profits. The inflows coincided with one of the strongest weekly rallies in benchmark indices: the Nifty rose 8.57% to close at 25,030 and the Sensex climbed 8.82% to settle at 81,028 on Friday, November 6.
items.title: FIIs pump Rs 45,960 crore into Indian stocks in a week; is the tide finally turning for Dalal Street?

items.summary: On Saturday evening, Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent Diwali greetings to India's people and reaffirmed his tradition of celebrating the festival with soldiers. He described the occasion as a symbol of the country's resolve against darkness and wished everyone happiness, peace and prosperity. Earlier that day he also exchanged greetings with Vice President CP Radhakrishnan.
items.title: Modi Sends Diwali Greetings and Promises to Keep Celebrating With Soldiers
